ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outside is square ABCD, with A at the upper left corner, B at the upper right corner, C at the lower right corner, and D at the lower left corner. Point E is located on the upper side AB and is close to A; point F is located on the right side BC; point G is located on the lower side CD; point H is located on the left side AD. The inner quadrilateral EFGH is drawn as a tilted square, with side EF going from E down to the right to F, and side FG going from F down to the left to G. Reasoning: The area of square ABCD is 100, so the side length is 10. Establish a coordinate system: let D=(0,0), C=(10,0), B=(10,10), A=(0,10). Because E is on AB and AE=2, E=(2,10). Suppose F is on the right side BC, and BF=t, then F=(10,10-t). Thus vector EF=(10-2,(10-t)-10)=(8,-t). Since EFGH is a square, FG is the adjacent side obtained by rotating EF by 90 degrees; according to the image, FG goes from F down to the left to G, so take the rotation vector FG=(-t,-8). Therefore the vertical drop from F to G is 8. Also because G is on the bottom side CD, the y-coordinate of F is 10-t, and the y-coordinate of G is 0, so the vertical drop from F to G is also 10-t. Thus 10-t=8, giving t=2. The area of square EFGH equals the side length squared, namely EF^2=8^2+2^2=64+4=68.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and square-side vectors. From the text, square ABCD has area 100, so its side length is 10. From the image, take A=(0,10), B=(10,10), C=(10,0), D=(0,0), with E on AB and AE=2, so E=(2,10). Let F be on the right side and write BF=t, so F=(10,10-t). Then vector EF=(8,-t). Since EFGH is a square, vector FG is a 90-degree rotation of EF, so its vertical component has magnitude 8. Because G lies on the bottom side in the image, the vertical drop from F to G must be 10-t, hence 10-t=8 and t=2. Therefore the area of square EFGH is EF^2=8^2+2^2=68.

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic offset/area-complement argument. From the text, the outer square side is 10, and from the image E splits the top side so AE=2 and EB=8. Because EFGH is a square with one vertex on each side of ABCD, rotating one side of the inner square by 90 degrees cycles the horizontal and vertical offsets around the outer square. Thus the short offset 2 and long offset 8 appear alternately on each side: the four corner regions AHE, BEF, CFG, and DGH are right triangles with legs 2 and 8. Each has area (1/2)(2)(8)=8. Subtract these four corner triangles from the outer square: area(EFGH)=100-4*8=68.
